intro.data: You already have readName and readAge from a Form. Build the single machine that produces the whole Record at once — so projecting it back out gives exactly readName and readAge.
intro.alchemy: You already have two extractions from a Seed. Build the single apparatus that produces the whole Compound at once — so projecting it back out gives exactly those extractions.
intro.spellcraft: You already have two draws from a Caster. Build the single rune that produces the whole Blend at once — so projecting it back out gives exactly those draws.
intro.abstract: Given f : X→A and g : X→B, build the unique pairing ⟨f,g⟩ : X→A×B so that π₁∘⟨f,g⟩ = f and π₂∘⟨f,g⟩ = g.

goal.data: Wire the Form through the pairing machine to build the Record.
goal.alchemy: Wire the Seed through the pairing apparatus to build the Compound.
goal.spellcraft: Wire the Caster through the pairing rune to build the Blend.
goal.abstract: Wire X through ⟨f,g⟩ to reach A×B.

afterSuccess.data: The pairing built the whole Record in one step, and projecting it gives back exactly readName and readAge. There is only one machine that does this — that uniqueness is what defines the product.
afterSuccess.alchemy: The pairing built the whole Compound in one step, and projecting it gives back exactly the two extractions. There is only one apparatus that does this — that uniqueness defines the product.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The pairing built the whole Blend in one step, and projecting it gives back exactly the two draws. There is only one rune that does this — that uniqueness defines the product.
afterSuccess.abstract: ⟨f,g⟩ builds the product in one step; the projections recover f and g. It is the unique such map — the universal property.

reveal.summary: The universal property of the product: for any f : X→A and g : X→B there is a unique ⟨f,g⟩ : X→A×B with π₁∘⟨f,g⟩ = f and π₂∘⟨f,g⟩ = g.
reveal.moreFormal: This universal property determines A×B up to isomorphism. The app confirms the two triangles commute; it trusts the author that the pairing is the unique one.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: x => ({ name: f(x), age: g(x) }) — and reading .name/.age gives f, g back.
